messages.text: Hello, it looks like I just hit the jackpot. How do I collect my 7.2 million bolts?
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill
Searched the web · Harlo pool bolts

I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Congrats on the big spin!

I can't see pool accounts, so I can't check your balance from here. This is how Bolts work, from our Harlo Pool page:

1. **What they are:** 
Bolts are the pool's prize points. Spins are the only way to get them, and they stack up in your pool account until you spend them in the Bolts store.
 They're not a coin, so nothing gets paid to your wallet.
2. **Check your balance:** Log in at pool.harlolabs.com with the email you signed up with. Your Bolts balance shows in your pool account.
3. **Spend them:** Open the Bolts store and pick the item you want. 
Confirm with 2FA and delivery is arranged by email. Stock is limited.


Your regular mining payouts are separate from Bolts. 
Your normal mining rewards are paid either way.


Can you see the 7.2 million Bolts in your pool account and the store when you log in? If something there doesn't look right, send me a screenshot and I'll take a look.
No, the 7.2 million bolts don't show up in my account.

Let's work out where that number came from. I can't see pool accounts, so I need to start with what you saw.

1. **Where did the 7.2 million Bolts show up?** Was it on the pool site after you hit Spin, or on your miner's own screen? Some Hammer units like the BC04 show the reels right on the display.
2. **Can you send a screenshot or photo of it?** If you have one, also send a screenshot of what your pool account shows now.

One quick thing to check while you look: make sure you're logged in at pool.harlolabs.com with the same email your miner's spins are linked to. If you have more than one login, the Bolts could be sitting in the other account.

Once I see the screenshots I can tell you what the next step is.
The URL I hit the jackpot on was: https://heliumdeploy.com/pages/harlo-pool
Read heliumdeploy.com/pages/harlo-pool
Handed to the team · Hal can't open that page or see pool accounts, so can't confirm whether the spin

Thanks, that helps. Here's what I know:

1. **Real Bolts are only won on the pool site.** Spin credits land in your account at pool.harlolabs.com, and one miner has to hold 800 GH/s on Harlo Pool for a full hour before you get any. Winning spins pay Bolts into that same account.
2. **The spin you hit was on our heliumdeploy.com page, not the pool site.** I can't open that page or see pool accounts from here, so I can't tell whether that spin was tied to your pool account. That would explain why the Bolts aren't showing.

I've passed this to the team so they can confirm exactly what that spin was. They're online now, and one of them will jump into this chat, so please stay here if you can. If you have to step away, they'll answer you by email.

While you wait: do you have a miner running on Harlo Pool right now? If so, which model is it?
Yes. Bitaxe.

Good, a Bitaxe works on Harlo Pool. Let's check that it actually qualifies for spins, because one miner has to hold 800 GH/s for a full hour. Depending on the model, some Bitaxes run close to that line or under it at stock settings.

Open your Bitaxe's dashboard (type its IP address into a browser) and tell me:

1. **Which Bitaxe it is** (Gamma, Supra, Ultra, etc.). It shows on the dashboard or the board.
2. **The hashrate it's showing**, ideally the average, not just the live number.
3. **The pool URL** under Settings, to confirm it's pointed at Harlo Pool.

A screenshot of the dashboard works too. If it's under 800 GH/s or the pool settings are off, that would explain why no spin credits or Bolts are reaching your pool account. The team is still on the jackpot question.
I believe it's a second or third generation Bitaxe.  It's labeled Bitaxe in gold lettering and has "401" in a smaller white text to the right of Bitaxe.
Searched the web · Bitaxe Supra 401 hashrate BM1368

Thanks, that label narrows it down. "401" is a board revision of the **Bitaxe Supra**, which runs on 
the BM1368 chip, with a typical hashrate of about 600 GH/s
 (from the ClusterAxe project's Bitaxe model table on GitHub).

That matters for spins: free spins need 
one miner holding 800 GH/s for an hour
, and 
two small miners don't add up, and a gap over 5 minutes restarts the hour
. A stock Supra usually sits below that line, so your Bitaxe may never have earned a spin credit in your pool account. That would also explain why no Bolts show up.

To confirm it, please do this one check:

1. Type the Bitaxe's IP address into a browser to open its dashboard.
2. Tell me the **average hashrate** it shows, or send a screenshot.

Please don't overclock it to reach 800 GH/s. The Supra wasn't built to run that hard on its stock cooler and power supply.

The team still has your question about the 7.2 million jackpot and will answer you here or by email.
It's been running for a couple of weeks now, and it shows 0 hashes.

Thanks, 0 hashes after a couple of weeks means the Bitaxe hasn't been doing any useful work. That also explains the missing spins: with no hashrate it can't reach 800 GH/s, so it never earns spin credits.

Where you see the 0 tells us what's wrong, so I need to know one thing:

**Where does it show 0?**
- **On the Bitaxe itself** (its small screen, or the dashboard you open by typing its IP into a browser): the miner isn't hashing at all. That points to power, the chip or settings.
- **On pool.harlolabs.com** (with the Bitaxe's own screen showing a number above 0): the miner is hashing but its work isn't reaching your pool account. That points to the pool settings.

A photo of the Bitaxe's small screen would help a lot. It usually shows the hashrate and the IP address.
On the dashboard it shows 0 hashes. My Bitaxe display isn't working correctly, so I can't read what's on it.

Thanks. If the Bitaxe's own dashboard shows 0, it isn't hashing at all. That's usually a power problem, or the miner can't reach the pool and so gets no work. The dashboard tells us which.

**Please send a screenshot of the whole dashboard page.** If you can't, read me these numbers off it:

1. **Power** (watts)
2. **Input voltage** (should be close to 5 V)
3. **ASIC temperature**
4. The **pool / stratum URL** and the **accepted shares** count

A Bitaxe that's working pulls real power and runs warm. If it shows close to 0 W and the chip is cool, that points to power. If it pulls power but shows no accepted shares, that points to the pool settings. The broken display could fit a power problem too, so these numbers will help.
The only metric the dashboard is showing is free ram.

Thanks, that's a useful clue. A dashboard that shows only free RAM, with no hashrate, power, voltage or temperature, usually means the Bitaxe's controller is running but isn't getting readings from the mining chip or its power circuit. With the display acting up too, I want to rule out power and firmware before anything else.

Please check two things:

1. **Is the fan spinning?** Yes or no is enough.
2. **Which firmware version is it running?** In AxeOS you'll find it on the **System** or **Settings** page, usually listed as "Version" or "AxeOS version". If you can, send a screenshot of that page plus the dashboard showing only free RAM.

If you can see a photo of the power supply's label, tell me what it says for output too (it should read **5V**). A wrong or weak power supply could cause both the blank readings and the display problem.
Fan is spinning. I just reset the miner to factory default settings.  Power supply is 5 volt, 5 amps, 25 watts.

Good, a spinning fan and a 5 V supply are what we want to see. The factory reset was a useful step, but it also wiped the Wi-Fi and pool settings, so we have to set the Bitaxe up again. These are the standard AxeOS steps:

1. **Connect to the Bitaxe's own Wi-Fi.** After a reset it creates its own hotspot. On your phone or laptop, look for a network whose name starts with **"Bitaxe"** and join it.
2. **Open the setup page.** In a browser go to **192.168.4.1**.
3. **Enter your home Wi-Fi.** Type in your network name and password. It has to be a **2.4 GHz** network, since the Bitaxe can't see 5 GHz.
4. **Enter the Harlo Pool settings:**
   - **Stratum URL and port:** copy these exactly as they appear on the Harlo Pool page or in your pool.harlolabs.com account.
   - **User / worker:** your BCH wallet address
   - **Password:** x
5. **Save and restart.** Then reconnect your phone or laptop to your home Wi-Fi.

Next, find the Bitaxe's new IP address in your router's device list (look for a device named "bitaxe"), open it in a browser and wait a few minutes.

Let me know what the dashboard shows after that. If hashrate, power and temperature show up, it was a settings problem. If you still see only free RAM, we'll try a different power supply next. The 25 W supply you have is on the low side, so it's worth ruling out.

The logs are a big help. Here's what they show:

1. **Network is fine.** The Bitaxe is online and reaching pools.
2. **It isn't pointed at Harlo Pool.** It's set to **solo.atlaspool.io** (pool 1) and **parasite.wtf** (pool 2). Those look like the factory default pools that came back with the reset.
3. **Both pools reject it.** "Authorization rejected" means the pool refused the username the Bitaxe sent. That usually happens when the User / worker field is empty or doesn't hold a valid address for that pool. With no pool accepting it, the Bitaxe gets no work, so it shows 0 hashrate.

To fix it, go to the Bitaxe's **Settings** (or **Pool**) page and set **pool 1** to Harlo Pool:
- **Stratum URL and port:** copy them exactly from the Harlo Pool page or your pool.harlolabs.com account
- **User:** your **BCH** wallet address. A Bitcoin (BTC) address won't work here.
- **Password:** x

For **pool 2**, either clear it or set it to Harlo Pool too. Then **save and restart**.

After a few minutes the logs should show "authorization accepted" (or similar) and then accepted shares, and the dashboard should start showing hashrate. Send me the new log lines once it's running.

Remember that a Supra usually runs around 600 GH/s, below the 800 GH/s that spins need. So even once it's mining properly on Harlo Pool, it may not earn spins. The team still has your jackpot question and will answer here or by email.

Progress! The pool side is fixed now:

- **"pool 2 connected to pool.harlolabs.com:8888"** and **"authorization accepted"**: Harlo Pool accepted your BCH address.
- **"new job"**: the pool is sending your Bitaxe work.

The new problem is on the board, right after each job arrives:

- **"probe_regulator: TPS546 ID"** and **"ASIC rails disabled"**: the firmware is looking for a **TPS546** voltage regulator, doesn't get the answer it expects, and so turns the chip's power off for safety. With the chip unpowered it can't hash, so the session ends and the cycle starts over.

The important detail is that a **Supra 401 doesn't use a TPS546**. Per the board notes in the AxeForge firmware release on GitHub, Supra boards 400/401 use a DS4432U, and only 402/403 use the TPS546. So the firmware seems to think it's on a different board. That points to a firmware or board-setting mismatch, possibly from the reset, rather than a dead board. I'm not sure of that yet, though, because I couldn't find these exact log lines documented anywhere.

**Two checks please, from the System or Settings page:**

1. **Firmware name and version.** Is it AxeOS, Harlo OS or something else, and which version number?
2. **Board version / device model.** Does it say **401**, or something else like 402, 403 or a Gamma model?

A screenshot of that page would be ideal. Please don't flash any other firmware yet. Once I know what it's running, I'll tell you exactly which official version to put on it.
I downloaded a firmware update from Harlo and it appears that Harlo flashed the wrong file for my Bitaxe.
Thanks, that explains the TPS546 lines. Let me check Harlo Labs' site to see which models and board revisions they support.

I think that's the cause. The firmware you flashed expects a TPS546 regulator, and your Supra 401 doesn't have one, so it turns off the chip's power before it can hash. The good news is that the firmware is shutting the power off as a safety step, and the pool connection works. So this looks like a firmware mismatch, not a broken Bitaxe.

I couldn't confirm from here whether Harlo OS has a profile for the Supra 401 specifically. I've passed your logs to JD, our hardware lead, who builds Harlo OS. He can tell you the right file to flash, or whether to go back to the Bitaxe's stock firmware. The team is online now and one of them will jump into this chat, so please stay here if you can. If you step away, you'll get the answer by email.

**For a faster answer:** join our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and mention **@nullhashrate** (that's JD) in the Harlo OS channel. He and the community are very active there.

1. **Which model did you pick in the Harlo flasher?** Tell me exactly what you selected from the list, or send a screenshot if it's still open.
2. **Please don't flash anything else for now**, so we fix it with the right file the first time.
